name: Cycle
description: Periodic return intelligence governing rhythmic recurrence, seasonal patterns, and oscillatory feedback loops across all living systems.

core_attributes.pattern: periodic recurrence, oscillatory feedback, rhythmic phase locking

scope.definition: Probability that a biological oscillator (circadian, cardiac, respiratory) returns to within 5% of its natural period within 10 cycles after a single-cycle external perturbation, averaged across oscillator types and species.

evidence.source: Pittendrigh (1960) 'Circadian rhythms and the circadian organization of living systems', Cold Spring Harbor Symposia 25:159-184; Strogatz (2003) 'Sync: The Emerging Science of Spontaneous Order', Hyperion; Glass (2001) 'Synchronization and rhythmic processes in physiology', Nature 410:277-284.
cross_domain_examples: circadian clock re-entrainment after jet lag: 3-10 day recovery to local period
cardiac pacemaker return to sinus rhythm after extrasystole (within 1-3 beats)
El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO): 3-7 year periodicity with post-event recovery
menstrual cycle re-entrainment after stress disruption (1-2 cycle recovery)
pendulum clock period recovery after impulse disturbance (physical analogue)

scope.falsifiability: If a biological oscillator is found where a single-cycle perturbation permanently shifts the period by >5% with no recovery over 10 cycles, phase-locking as a universal biological oscillator property fails for that system.
scope.measurement_limits: Phase-lock fidelity decreases with perturbation magnitude — perturbations >50% of natural period may not recover. Measured in isolated oscillator systems; coupled oscillators (e.g., circadian + cardiac) may show faster recovery through mutual entrainment.
